text:
sara: Heads-up: a customer (Acme) reported missing rows in console CSV export for audit logs — they say events older than page 1 vanish when they filter by KMS key usage. Repro steps attached.

mike: Uh — do we have any known pagination + RBAC edgecases? I thought export was server-side paginated and then stitched.

sara: Repro: in Console -> Audit -> Filter: resource:kms_key_id:<id> -> Set time range 90d -> click Export CSV -> download contains only first 1000 rows, but UI shows ~3k rows. If user is an org.viewer (no export role) they still see Export button, download happens but truncated. Paste of response headers:

```
GET /api/audit/export?filter=...&page=1
x-total-count: 3178
content-range: items 0-999/3178
```

And server returns 200 for subsequent pages but join step fails, resulting file only has first page.

alina: That's bad. Product: we shouldn't expose Export to roles that don't have export permission. Is this a frontend leak or backend skips checks on paged fetches?

mike: Backend bug: export worker assumes caller has export scope when stitching pages; there's an auth-check on initial request but not on subsequent page fetches from the worker. Worker runs with caller token scoped to first page only — if restricted, subsequent pages return 403 and worker silently stops. I'll open a PR.

jon: Can we add defensive validation in backend: when stitching, verify total pages fetched == x-total-count / pageSize and if mismatch return 500 + telemetry? Also have the UI validate that downloaded rows == shown rows and show a warning.

sara: Also schema issue reported: some customers see audit_event.kms_key_id missing in JSON export for older events — looks like schema v2 added kms_key_id as top-level field, older rows still have it nested under details.kms. We need export to normalize to current schema for customer-facing downloads.

tara: Support: customer hit compliance audit — they reported the missing kms_key_id and truncated CSV. We promised a mitigation: a one-off full export scoped to their org. Who owns that? I can coordinate but need secure access.

mike: I'll do the mitigation with a temporary admin token; we should log the export event and require approval. Also long-term: worker fix + auth check + schema normalization pipeline.

alina: Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- backend: require export permission on every page fetch; fail fast with clear error
- backend: normalize legacy audit rows to canonical schema in exports (kms_key_id, principal_id, action)
- frontend: hide Export button when user lacks export role; display clear error if downloaded rows < expected
- telemetry: capture export_attempt, export_stitched_pages, export_failure_reason
- docs: update Console Export docs to mention pagination limits and RBAC

jon: I'll prototype UI change. Suggest "Export scope" dropdown: current view / time range / full org (admin only). Also add a "preview first 500 rows" modal to validate before download.

mike: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/9876 (wip). Code snippet for auth check:

```
if (!caller.hasPermission('audit.export')) {
  throw new ForbiddenError('export requires audit.export')
}
```

sara: For KMS schema normalization, note: don't accidentally surface raw key material; only show key_id and usage. KMS fields must be redacted if the key is customer-managed with redaction flag.

tara: Please keep me posted so I can tell the customer ETA.

audit-bot: Created incident INC-2026-45: audit-export-truncate — assigned to mike, severity: P2.

sara: Thanks. mike — can you include a temporary mitigation step we can run for affected customers? Post the script here and I'll validate with security.

mike: Will do, ETA EOD. Quick mitigation script below (runs as admin):

```
# stream all pages and write canonical csv
for page in range(1, 10000):
  r = admin_client.fetch_audit_page(org_id, filter, page)
  if r.status == 403:
    raise Exception('permission denied while stitching')
  write_rows(r.items)
  if end_of_pages: break
```

I'll make it safe: require MFA approval and audit-bot confirmation.

sara: Great. tagging @security-leads for visibility. :eyes:
